payload.root_cause: In camelCase (src/text.js:36-44), the per-word capitalization at line 41 uses the wrong character index: `lower[1].toUpperCase() + lower.slice(1)` upper-cases the SECOND letter of each word (and keeps the original first letter lowercase via `lower.slice(1)`, which starts at index 1 but the wrongly-uppercased second char replaces nothing — it is prepended). For 'big' it produces 'I' + 'ig' = 'Iig' (dropping the 'b' and uppercasing 'i'), and for 'world' 'O' + 'orld' = 'Oorld' (dropping 'w'). Hence camelCase('hello big world') returns 'helloIigOorld' instead of 'helloBigWorld'. The correct expression is `lower[0].toUpperCase() + lower.slice(1)`.

payload.rationale: The root cause is an off-by-one index in the capitalization expression for non-initial words in camelCase: `lower[1].toUpperCase() + lower.slice(1)` upper-cases the second character of each word and drops the first character entirely (e.g. 'big' -> 'I' + 'ig' = 'Iig'). Changing the index from 1 to 0 makes it uppercase the first character and keep the remainder via `lower.slice(1)`, producing 'Big', so camelCase('hello big world') correctly returns 'helloBigWorld' as documented. No other code is affected since this is the only use of that expression.
